first_impression.reaction: Fine. It says straight up who it's for and that it's going to walk through the steps in order. No 'magical day' fluff. The key takeaways give me a dated Smartraveller rating in the first screen, which tells me someone actually checked something. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, then went back through it.

journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Lebanon "Do not travel" (as at November 2026), so this guide is about bringing the customs to a wedding elsewhere.
journey.reaction: Good. A named source and a date. And they're honest about why they aren't selling me a wedding in Beirut. That's the opposite of marketing hiding the catch.

journey.quote: Britannica lists Shia and Sunni Muslims as Lebanon's two largest religious groups, with Maronite Christians making up more than one-fifth of the population
journey.reaction: Sourced, checkable. I can verify that in thirty seconds, which is the point.

journey.quote: that account is framed around Muslim families in Egypt, Palestine and Jordan rather than Lebanon.
journey.reaction: Admitting the source isn't exactly about Lebanon. Most sites would just paste it in. I respect that.

journey.quote: It is often told as a sign of strength and of the couple cutting the first piece of their new life together, though families tell it in different ways.
journey.reaction: 'Often told' turns up a lot in this part (zaffeh, zaghareet, sword, almonds) with no source behind it, while the earlier sections cite Britannica and the churches. Not a dealbreaker, it's honest hedging, but it reads like the research ran out halfway.

journey.section: Space for the zaffeh and the dabke line
journey.quote: Ask the venue for the floor's real dimensions once tables are set, and whether a terrace can take the overflow.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. A concrete question I can actually put in my spreadsheet and ask three venues.

journey.section: Space for the zaffeh and the dabke line
journey.quote: Not published: music finish times and percussion rules for most shortlisted venues. Your Wedded Advisor confirms these with the venue in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Telling me what isn't known, and that it gets confirmed in writing. That's what I want from a planner. 'Shortlisted venues' is a bit odd though, whose shortlist? I haven't got one from them.

journey.section: Blades, venue rules and the cake
journey.quote: Your Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel and vendors, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms what is included in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Better than most. Fee in writing up front, inclusions in writing. But what's the fee model? Flat fee, percentage, or do you take a cut from the venue? That's my first question and it isn't here.

journey.section: A note on travel and marriage law
journey.quote: This is general information, not legal advice. Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm a marriage's validity.
journey.reaction: Honest about limits. Not overselling. Good.

journey.section: Bringing Lebanese customs to a wedding abroad
journey.quote: For two real examples, see [a traditional Lebanese wedding on Lake Como] and [a Lebanese couple's medieval-style wedding in Italy].
journey.reaction: Real weddings, fine. But I'll click and I'll be looking for guest numbers and an actual budget. If it's just pretty photos, that's a miss.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage of spend, or commission from venues and suppliers?
Do you take a cut from the venue or mark up supplier prices?
What does a Lebanese-style wedding for roughly 200 to 300 guests in Italy actually cost, even as a range from a real wedding?
Which venues have you actually confirmed can take a zaffeh with live drums and a long dabke floor?
Is there any independent proof (reviews, named couples) behind the real-wedding links?
would_share_with: My partner's family, for the order of events and the 'ask both families early' point

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like one person to hold all of this together, you can speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the useful content, not before, and it's low-pressure, so it doesn't annoy me. The 'fee agreed in writing' line helps. I'd still want the fee model and the commission question answered before I hand over my details, so I'd click through to see what the next page says rather than enquire straight away.

top_3_changes: Back the celebration section claims (zaffeh, sword, sugared almonds, zaghareet) with at least one source each, the way the ceremony section does, or say plainly that these are family-reported customs.
Change 'for most shortlisted venues' to something that doesn't assume I already have a shortlist from you, e.g. 'for most venues'.
Next to the Advisor line, link to wherever the fee model and supplier pricing policy are explained, once that page exists (deferred business detail, not a must-fix here).
